summary: The multiple-scattering sanity benchmark of geant4_benchmarks.py divided the RMS of the central 98 % of the projected exit angles by 0.8673 (close to the truncated variance) instead of 0.9346, the RMS of a unit Gaussian truncated to its central 98 %: its core width was 7.8 % high for exactly Gaussian angles.

observables: the core width (geant4) and relative_difference of the multiple-scattering sanity benchmark
impact.bias: +7.8 % on the core width (0.93459 / 0.8673) whatever the angles; most of the +11 % that VALIDATION GEANT4-F4 recorded for RMS(central 98 %) / 0.8673 against Lynch and Dahl is this factor (about +3 % with the correct one)
impact.trigger: a geant4_benchmarks.py run with a multiple-scattering benchmark; multiple-scattering-reference (the truncated-normal fit) is not affected

applies_to.match_basis: a Geant4 study record (check_geant4_study.py) embeds the benchmark results of geant4_benchmarks.py in extension.study.benchmarks; a record that lists one of these benchmarks was evaluated by the affected code

outputs.how_to_recognize: geant4_benchmarks.py run output (JSON) whose benchmarks list holds benchmark multiple-scattering

remedy: rerun geant4_benchmarks.py on the same CSVs with this version; the sanity verdict can change for widths within about 8 % of the 20 % window edge
